check: hunt for assertions that can never fail, the shape already found three times this session
why: A check that always passes is worse than no check, because it is counted. Three instances surfaced earlier - a gate threshold too strict to ever pass a failure through, an offline-build claim that could not go stale, and a jar selection that would have hashed the sources jar consistently. This looked for a fourth in the test suite.

whatWasRuledOut.triviallyTrueAssertions: Searching for assertTrue(true), assertFalse(false) and assertEquals with identical arguments returns nothing across all four test source sets.
whatWasRuledOut.scanValidated: assertTrue( appears 843 times, so the search works and the zero is real.

whatWasFound.shape: Filtered-stream assertions whose filtered subset is never asserted non-empty
whatWasFound.whyTheyCanPassVacuously: allMatch on an empty stream is true. If the compiled component contains no walkable voxels, both assertions hold without examining anything.
whatWasFound.theGuardsPresentDoNotCoverIt: GateCapTest asserts c.voxels() is non-empty, and WallDecayTest asserts both that and that some solid voxel has x > 0. Neither pins the walkable subset. SupportGraph.reachable, the assertion above GateCapTest line 71, works from occupancy rather than from VoxelIntent.walkable, so it does not imply any walkable voxel exists.
whatWasFound.whyItMattersForGateCapTestSpecifically: The test is named capHasGroundEgressAndDoesNotKeepAnIsolatedTip. Its subject is that a ground egress exists, which is a walkable path - so if the filter selected nothing, the test would pass while asserting nothing about the very thing it is named for.

whatWouldCloseIt: An assertion that the walkable subset is non-empty, or that at least one walkable voxel sits on each side the assertion cares about. That would make the allMatch test something.
severity: Low as a product matter and moderate as an evidence matter. Nothing here suggests the two tests currently pass vacuously, since both components are expected to have walkable voxels. The gap is that a regression removing them would not be caught, and the test would still be counted as coverage.
head: 61a9650

theKeyQuestionSettled.question: In GateCapTest, the assertion above line 71 is that SupportGraph.reachable holds between two points. Does that imply at least one walkable voxel exists, which would make line 71 meaningful after all?
theKeyQuestionSettled.evidence: standable, which reachable walks over, tests the floor voxel against structural(floor) and checks clearance above. It never consults VoxelIntent.walkable. The two predicates are different, so a component can be traversable in the support graph while containing no voxel the filter at line 71 would select.
theKeyQuestionSettled.consequence: The assertion at line 71 can pass on an empty stream with no help from the surrounding assertions.

whatRemainsOpen: Whether the two components currently produce walkable voxels. Nothing in the results distinguishes a real pass from a vacuous one - both tests report zero failures either way. That is exactly the gap: the tests are counted as coverage for behaviour they would not notice losing.
